claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 can be processed into a single-phase metastable high-temperature BCC state.
The composition of Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 sets the Gibbs free-energy difference between BCC and a competing phase.
The phase stability of Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is governed by the BCC-to-secondary-phase free-energy difference.
At the relevant intermediate temperature, the competing secondary phase has lower free energy than BCC.
A sufficiently long intermediate-temperature hold allows the thermodynamic driving force to overcome diffusion-related kinetic limitations and trigger secondary-phase nucleation and growth.
Rapid quenching to multiple intermediate temperatures followed by systematically varied isothermal holds is the proposed intervention.
CALPHAD estimates identify a thermodynamic-instability threshold for the target Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 composition.
The secondary phase may nucleate both at grain boundaries and within grains.
An Al-containing Cr-Co-Fe-Ni alloy can form an intermetallic L12 secondary phase during intermediate-temperature isothermal treatment.
The transformation will have a distinct onset at a specific hold time and temperature.
Transformation onset will be observed as a reduction in BCC phase fraction and appearance of a secondary phase.
The phase-fraction change will be reproducible under the same time-temperature conditions.
Transformation onset will correlate with the predicted Gibbs free-energy threshold.
The controlled baseline consists of identically processed, composition-matched BCC samples that receive no hold at the proposed critical intermediate temperatures.
The proposed mechanism operates only within a narrow temperature-time window.
Excessively rapid quenching can suppress transformation because diffusion is kinetically limited.
At temperatures far from the proposed threshold, transformation is absent because either thermodynamic driving force is insufficient or kinetic barriers are too large.
The magnitude of the critical Gibbs free-energy difference and the identity of the secondary phase are not yet specified.
Failure to observe a distinct onset within the predicted window, transformation outside that window, or continuous transformation without a threshold would falsify the hypothesis.
